critical_operation.code_excerpt:
template_file = Path(directory) / template
                if template_file.exists():
                    with template_file.open() as f:
                        template_contents = f.read()
critical_operation.description: TemplateDetailView.get_context_data takes `template` from self.kwargs (the URL) and joins it onto each configured template directory with pathlib's `/` operator at line 331, with no sanitation. An absolute value such as '/etc/passwd' makes pathlib discard `directory`, and a value such as '../passwd' escapes it; the following template_file.exists() (332, 340) then reports the existence of the targeted file and the file is opened and read into template_contents (333-334), which is placed in the context (341). The stock template_detail.html only renders the path and the exists flag, but the advisory notes that a customized admindocs template that renders `template.contents` exposes the contents too. The fix replaces the join with Path(safe_join(directory, template)), so a path outside the template directory raises SuspiciousFileOperation and yields HTTP 400 (the added regression test asserts 400 for '/etc/passwd' and '../passwd').

entry_point.description: The route 'templates/<path:template>/' captures the URL segment with the <path:...> converter, which matches slashes and a leading slash, and passes it as the template kwarg to TemplateDetailView. The admindocs URLs are only active when the project installs django.contrib.admindocs and includes admindocs.urls.

source_crosscheck.notes: The CNA (mitre) gives the affected versions and the description but no CVSS and no CWE. NVD supplies its own Primary CVSS 3.1 4.9 MEDIUM and CWE-22, so it is an independent assessment rather than a mirror. OSV/GHSA repeats the 3.1 vector, adds a CVSS 4.0 vector, severity MODERATE and the same CWE. All published severity levels are MEDIUM/MODERATE (4.9); no level conflict. The git evidence matches the advisory ranges: 3.0.2 and 3.0.14 carry the vulnerable blob, 3.1.12 and 3.2.4 carry the fixed blob and the fix commits are ancestors of their release commits.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read django/contrib/admindocs/views.py at 3.0.2 and confirm line 331 joins the URL-derived template path onto the template directory without safe_join.

An independent reviewer must confirm the <path:template> route supplies an unsanitized value and that the following exists()/read exposes arbitrary file existence (and contents with a customized template).
An independent reviewer must confirm 20c67a06/dfaba12c are the fixes, that they are ancestors of 3.1.12/3.2.4, and that 3.0.14 is still unfixed.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No code was executed: the traversal is read from the pathlib join and the fix, not reproduced, and no HTTP request was made.

django.contrib.admindocs is an optional application and BaseAdminDocsView.dispatch requires a staff account (staff_member_required at views.py:33); projects without admindocs installed or without a staff user are not exposed.

The stock admin_doc/template_detail.html renders only template.file and the exists flag, so with unmodified templates the impact is file-existence disclosure; content disclosure requires the customized template described in the advisory.
Only 3.1.12 and 3.2.4 were content-verified as fixed; the 2.2.24 fix (053cc953) is recorded from the advisory/OSV and was not content-verified here.

The 3.0.x line never received a fixed release (3.0.14 still carries blob 0474c38f), so users of this snapshot must upgrade to 3.1.12/3.2.4 or later; the dataset records the flaw at 3.0.2 without a same-line fixed release.
The CNA record carries no CVSS or CWE; severity and CWE rest on NVD (Primary) and GHSA, which agree.
The advisory gives no reporter or reproduction reference, so no independent reproduction is available and grade A is not attainable.
open_questions: Whether the Django exception handler in every supported deployment maps SuspiciousFileOperation to 400 (the regression test asserts 400, which implies it in the test settings) was not verified outside the test.
The advisory does not enumerate which customized admin templates would render contents; that exposure depends on the project's own template.
Whether the 2.2.24 fix is byte-equivalent to the 3.1.12/3.2.4 fix was not content-verified; only the 3.1/3.2 trees were read.
